rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects the preceding interpretations as unsupported departures from the wording; reading this part as janāba would repeat the ruling already stated.
rows.anchor: كل ما ذكروه عدول عن ظاهر اللفظ بغير دليل ، فوجب أن لا يجوز . وأيضا فحكم الجنابة تقدم في قوله : { ولا جنبا }

rows.speaker: أهل الظاهر
rows.claim: The literalists hold that only the person who touches a woman loses ablution; the person touched does not.
rows.anchor: قال أهل الظاهر : إنما ينتقض وضوء اللامس لظاهر قوله

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that both the toucher and the person touched lose ablution.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : بل ينتقض وضوءهما معا

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires a fresh search for water when each prayer time begins after a person has prayed using tayammum, since not finding it implies prior searching.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : إذا دخل وقت الصلاة فطلب الماء ولم يجده وتيمم وصلى

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds that a person who already searched and prayed with tayammum need not search again when the next prayer time begins.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه لا يجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says the verb found does not itself imply prior searching, as Qur’anic uses of finding describe matters for which searching by God is impossible.
rows.anchor: قولنا : وجد ، لا يشعر بسبق الطلب ، بدليل قوله تعالى : { ووجدك ضالا فهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that divine seeking is figurative: God singled out Muḥammad and commanded people, whose failure is like seeking something and not finding it.
rows.anchor: الطلب وإن كان في حقه تعالى محالا ، إلا أنه لما أخرج محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم من بين قومه بما لم يكن لائقا لقومه صار ذلك كأنه طلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is consensus that someone who has water but needs it for their own thirst or that of a protected animal may perform tayammum.
rows.anchor: أجمعوا على أنه لو وجد الماء لكنه يحتاج إليه لعطشه أو عطش حيوان محترم جاز له التيمم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires using any available amount insufficient for full ablution together with tayammum, relying on the verse’s apparent wording.
rows.anchor: قد أوجبه الشافعي رضي الله عنه ، متمسكا بظاهر لفظ الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammum means intending or aiming; the forms ammamtuhu, tayammamtuhu, and taʾammamtuhu all mean I intended it.
rows.anchor: التيمم في اللغة عبارة عن القصد ، يقال : أممته وتيممته وتأممته ، أي قصدته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains ṣaʿīd as the face of the earth, whether soil or another material.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : الصعيد وجه الأرض ، ترابا كان أو غيره

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa permits tayammum by striking and wiping on bare rock without dust, since ṣaʿīd means what rises from the earth and the command is to intend land.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه : لو فرضنا صخرا لا تراب عليه فضرب المتيمم يده عليه ومسح كان ذلك كافيا

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires soil that sticks to the hand for tayammum.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : بل لا بد من تراب يلتصق بيده

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that the unrestricted wording here is restricted by 5:6, where min in wiping from it indicates taking a portion of soil; al-Kashshāf says Arabs understand such phrasing partitivally.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : لا يفهم أحد من العرب من قول القائل : مسحت برأسه من الدهن ومن الماء ومن التراب : إلا معنى التبعيض

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī argues that good earth is earth that grows plants, as 7:58 says, so the command to use good ṣaʿīd requires soil rather than barren rock.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره الواحدي رحمه الله ، وهو أنه تعالى أوجب في هذه الآية كون الصعيد طيبا ، والأرض الطيبة هي التي تنبت بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī favors soil as the cautious meaning of good ṣaʿīd: non-saline earth, whose use is agreed valid, is specified in Prophetic reports as purifier.
rows.anchor: وجب حمل الصعيد الطيب عليه رعاية لقاعدة الاحتياط ، لا سيما وقد خصص النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام التراب بهذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī argues that paired denial and affirmation must share a modality: forgiveness below shirk is gracious, not obligatory; on the Muʿtazilite premise that minor and repentant major sins must be forgiven, the verse concerns major sins before repentance.
rows.anchor: وجب أن يكون قوله : { ويغفر ما دون ذلك } هو أن يغفره على سبيل التفضل

words: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since everything besides shirk includes major sins before and after repentance and minor sins, the verse’s promise of forgiveness subject to will includes major sins before repentance.
rows.anchor: وجب أن تكون الكبيرة قبل التوبة أيضا مغفورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because minor sins and major sins after repentance are certainly forgiven rather than left to discretion, the phrase about whom God wills must refer to major sins before repentance.
rows.anchor: وغفران الكبيرة بعد التوبة وغفران الصغيرة مقطوع به ، وغير معلق على المشيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says that making forgiveness depend on God’s will does not rule out its being obligatory, just as God purifies only those fit for purification in 4:49.
rows.anchor: اعترضوا على هذا الوجه الأخير بأن تعليق الأمر بالمشيئة لا ينافي وجوبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the threat about shirk, Jews claimed special status as God’s children and beloved, expected only brief punishment, and said only Jews or Christians enter Paradise; some relied on prophetic ancestors to intercede.
rows.anchor: لسنا من المشركين ، بل نحن خواص الله تعالى كما حكى تعالى عنهم انه قالوا : { نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Jews brought children to the Prophet and, after he said the children were sinless, claimed that their own day and night’s deeds canceled each other out.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أن قوما من اليهود أتوا بأطفالهم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiya here means a person praising themself, like a witness being declared upright; because piety is inward and only God knows it, only God can truly purify.
rows.anchor: التزكية في هذا الموضع عبارة عن مدح الإنسان نفسه ، ومنه تزكية المعدل للشاهد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked how the Prophet could call himself trustworthy in heaven and earth, Rāzī answers that he said this after hypocrites challenged his fairness and God had authenticated him by a miracle.
rows.anchor: أليس أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( والله إني لأمين في السماء أمين في الأرض )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since faith is the greatest and noblest purification, God’s saying that He purifies whom He wills shows that He creates believers’ faith.
rows.anchor: دل على أن إيمان المؤمنين لم يحصل إلا بخلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No injustice by even a thread can mean either that self-praisers receive their due punishment without injustice or that those God purifies receive their full reward.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ان الذين يزكون أنفسهم يعاقبون على تلك التزكية حق جزائهم من غير ظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, those whom God purifies are rewarded for their obedience without any reduction in reward.
rows.anchor: أن الذين زكاهم الله فإنه يثيبهم على طاعاتهم ولا ينقص من ثوابهم شيئا

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Fatīl can be the grime twisted between fingers; Ibn al-Sikkīt defines it as the groove in a date stone, while naqīr is its dot and quṭmīr its thin covering; all denote something tiny.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن السكيت : الفتيل ما كان في شق النواة ، والنقير النقطة التي في ظهر النواة ، والقطمير القشرة الرقيقة على النواة

words: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to look expresses amazement at their lies about God, including their self-purification, claims of being His children and beloved, and exclusive entitlement to Paradise.
rows.anchor: هذا تعجيب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من فريتهم على الله ، وهي تزكيتهم أنفسهم وافتراؤهم على الله

words: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says a report is false whenever it contradicts reality, whether its speaker knows that or not; the Jews’ mistaken self-belief does not make their claims true.
rows.anchor: مذهبنا أن الخبر عن الشيء إذا كان على خلاف المخبر عنه كان كذبا ، سواء علم قائله كونه كذلك أو لم يعلم

words: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب
rows.speaker: الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ holds that a statement is a lie only if its speaker knows that it contradicts reality; Rāzī rejects this view using the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال الجاحظ : شرط كونه كذبا أن يعلم كونه بخلاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression kāfā bihi intensifies either praise or blame, and in this passage it is used for blame.
rows.anchor: وإنما يقال : كفى به في التعظيم على جهة المدح أو على جهة الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative phrase ithman mubīnan is a tamyīz, a specification in the construction.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { إثما مبينا } منصوب على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After threatening a particular group among the People of the Book, the passage states the threat that applies to disbelievers generally.
rows.anchor: بعدما ذكر الوعيد بالطائفة الخاصة من أهل الكتاب بين ما يعم الكافرين من الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs include everything indicating His essence, acts, attributes, and names, as well as angels, scriptures, and messengers.
rows.anchor: يدخل في الآيات كل ما يدل على ذات الله وأفعاله وصفاته وأسمائه والملائكة والكتب والرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief in the signs can mean denying their status as signs, neglecting to consider them, raising doubts about them, or knowingly rejecting them out of obstinacy and envy; Rāzī discussed disbelief at 2:6.
rows.anchor: وكفرهم بالآيات ليس يكون بالجحد ، لكن بوجوه ، منها أن ينكروا كونها آيات ، ومنها أن يغفلوا عنها

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says sawfa signals threat and warning, with sīn serving similarly; it can also introduce promises, but both particles are specific to the future.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه : ( سوف ) كلمة تذكر للتهديد والوعيد ، يقال : سوف أفعل ، وينوب عنها حرف السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṣlīhim means to make them enter the Fire and also carries the added sense of roasting them, as one says a roasted sheep.
rows.anchor: قوله : { نصليهم } أي ندخلهم النار ، لكن قوله : { نصليهم } فيه زيادة على ذلك فانه بمنزلة شويته بالنار ، يقال شاة مصلية أي مشوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked why God does not preserve their bodies from burning, Rāzī answers that God is not questioned about His acts and can inflict immense pain without fire, though He places them in fire.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى لا يسأل عما يفعل ، بل نقول : انه تعالى قادر على أن يوصل إلى أبدانهم آلاما عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī raises the justice objection that replacing burned skin with new skin would punish skin that did not commit the sin.
rows.anchor: هذا تعذيبا لمن لم يعص وهو غير جائز .

words: كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُم بَدَّلْنَٰهُمْ جُلُودًا غَيْرَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer treats ripeness as a changed attribute of the same skin-subject, so the person punished remains the same and the change is only in quality.
rows.anchor: أن يجعل النضج غير النضيج ، فالذات واحدة والمتبدل هو الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer says the human being is punished and skin is an attached addition, not part of the human essence; renewing it therefore does not punish someone else.
rows.anchor: المعذب هو الإنسان ، وذلك الجلد ما كان جزأ من ماهية الإنسان ، بل كان كالشيء الملتصق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes skins as garments, so their renewal refers to clothing; it cites the garments of tar in 14:50.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالجلود السرابيل ، قال تعالى : { سرابيلهم من قطران } ( إبراهيم : 50 )

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī rejects the garment interpretation as abandoning the apparent wording and says tar garments are described as burning, not ripening.
rows.anchor: طعن القاضي فيه ، فقال : إنه ترك للظاهر ، وأيضا السرابيل من القطران لا توصف بالنضج

words: كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُم بَدَّلْنَٰهُمْ جُلُودًا غَيْرَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth possibility reads the skin renewal as a metaphor for unending torment: whenever the damned seem to have reached death, they receive renewed life and suffering continues.
rows.anchor: هذا استعارة عن الدوام وعدم الانقطاع ، كما يقال لمن يراد وصفه بالدوام : كلما انتهى فقد ابتدأ

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says God makes replacement skin from the unbeliever’s own flesh; Rāzī calls this unlikely because the finite flesh would eventually run out and another mechanism is not explained.
rows.anchor: قال السدي : إنه تعالى يبدل الجلود من لحم الكافر فيخرج من لحمه جلدا آخر وهذا بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-yadhūqū means that their tasting of punishment continues without interruption, like a wish that someone remain in and increase in honor.
rows.anchor: أي ليدوم لهم ذوقه ولا ينقطع ، كقولك للمعزوز : أعزك الله ، أي أدامك على العز وزادك فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can also mean they taste the punishment in their renewed state, since they are already continuously tasting it.
rows.anchor: وأيضا المراد ليذوقوا بهذه الحالة الجديدة العذاب ، وإلا فهم ذائقون مستمرون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This third set of rulings follows the permission to enjoy lawful good things in 5:87–88 by clarifying that wine and gambling are prohibited rather than lawful.
rows.anchor: وجه اتصاله بما قبله أنه تعالى قال فيما تقدم { لا تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One etymology says wine is called khamr because it mixes with and veils the mind.
rows.anchor: سميت الخمر خمرا لأنها خامرت العقل ، أي خالطته فسترته

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī offers another etymology: it was left to ferment and change its smell.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي : تركت فاختمرت ، أي تغير ريحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir is their gambling over a camel; anṣāb are idols set up for worship; azlām are arrows marked good and bad. Rāzī points to his earlier explanations in 5:3 and Sūrat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: الميسر هو قمارهم في الجزور ، والأنصاب هي آلهتهم التي نصبوها يعبدونها ، والأزلام سهام مكتوب عليها خير وشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī directs readers to his earlier discussion of anṣāb and azlām at 5:3, and of wine and gambling in Sūrat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وذكرنا معنى الأنصاب والأزلام في أول هذه السورة عند قوله } وما ذبح على النصب وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs means anything abominable in action; its root suggests a forceful sound, as in thunderous clouds, so it denotes conduct powerfully and completely foul.
rows.anchor: الرجس في اللغة كل ما استقذر من عمل . يقال : رجس الرجل رجسا ورجس إذا عمل عملا قبيحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling these things Satan’s work intensifies their ugliness: Satan and disbelievers are impure, the impure invite only to the impure, and attribution to Satan stresses extreme repugnance.
rows.anchor: كل ما أضيف إلى الشيطان فالمراد من تلك الإضافة المبالغة في كمال قبحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical reading makes the pronoun in اجتنبوه refer to rijs, whose scope covers all four prohibited things.
rows.anchor: أنها عائدة إلى الرجس ، والرجس واقع على الأربعة المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to an omitted noun such as the conduct or handling of wine and gambling.
rows.anchor: أنها عائدة إلى المضاف المحذوف ، كأنه قيل : إنما شأن الخمر والميسر أو تعاطيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse names worldly harms of wine and gambling: Satan seeks to create enmity and hatred between people and distract them from remembering God and prayer.
rows.anchor: ذكر فيها نوعين من المفسدة : فالأول : ما يتعلق بالدنيا وهو قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the pronoun in kadhdhaba bihi back to the punishment in the previous verse, which is true and must descend on them.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنه راجع إلى العذاب المذكور في الآية السابقة { وهو الحق } أي لا بد وأن ينزل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes the pronoun as referring to the Qur’an, true as a book revealed by God.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الضمير في ( به ) للقرآن وهو الحق أي في كونه كتابا منزلا من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view makes the pronoun refer to the ordering of signs, whose status as proofs the people denied.
rows.anchor: الثالث : يعود إلى تصريف الآيات وهو الحق لأنهم كذبوا كون هذه الأشياء دلالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not their keeper or guardian who must punish their denial and refusal of proofs; he is a warner, while God judges their deeds.
rows.anchor: أي لست عليكم بحافظ حتى أجازيكم على تكذيبكم وإعراضكم عن قبول الدلائل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and the commentators say the statement was abrogated by the fighting verse; Rāzī regards that claim as far-fetched.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون : نسختها آية القتال وهو بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustaqar may be a place of settlement or the settlement itself; forms derived from verbs beyond triliteral can have a passive-participle pattern used for verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: والمستقر يجوز أن يكون موضع الاستقرار ، ويجوز أن يكون نفس الاستقرار لأن ما زاد على الثلاثي كان المصدر منه على زنة اسم المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every divine report has a time or place when it will occur without failure or delay; on the verbal-noun reading every promise and threat must come to fulfillment.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن لكل خبر يخبره الله تعالى وقتا أو مكانا يحصل فيه من غير خلف ولا تأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning to the disbelievers may refer either to punishment in the Hereafter or to the Muslims’ worldly ascendancy over them by war, killing, and subjugation.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي خوف الكفار به ، يجوز أن يكون المراد منه عذاب الآخرة ، ويجوز أن يكون المراد منه استيلاء المسلمين على الكفار

none: source fragment breaks off mid-quotation before commentary

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous verse says the Messenger need not stay with deniers; this verse adds that when they mock the religion and attack the Messenger, believers must avoid their company.
rows.anchor: الذين يكذبون بهذا الدين فإنه لا يجب على الرسول أن يلازمهم وأن يكون حفيظا عليهم ثم بين في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the address as directed to the Prophet, with others intended by the command.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد غيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view addresses someone other than the Prophet, namely any listener who sees people mocking the signs.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب لغيره أي إذا رأيت أيها السامع الذين يخوضون في آياتنا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī reports that polytheists insulted and mocked the Prophet and Qur’an when sitting with believers, so they were ordered to leave until the subject changed.
rows.anchor: ونقل الواحدي أن المشركين كانوا إذا جالسوا المؤمنين وقعوا في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawḍ means engaging in conversation frivolously or playfully; saying people were left khāʾiḍūn implies they had started saying things that should not be said.
rows.anchor: ولفظ الخوض في اللغة عبارة عن المفاوضة على وجه العبث واللعب ، قال تعالى حكاية عن الكفار : { وكنا نخوض مع الخائضين }

rows.speaker: الحشوية
rows.claim: The Ḥashwiyya use this verse to prohibit theological reasoning and debate about God’s essence and attributes, calling it forbidden engagement with His signs.
rows.anchor: ومن الحشوية من تمسك بهذه الآية في النهي عن الاستدلال والمناظرة في ذات الله تعالى وصفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects that argument: exegetes and the language use khawḍ here for entering into the signs to attack or mock them, not reasoned theological debate.
rows.anchor: أنا نقلنا عن المفسرين أن المراد من ( الخوض ) الشروع في آيات الله تعالى على سبيل الطعن والاستهزاء

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads yunsiyannaka with a doubled nūn; form II and form IV can function alike, as in the example from 74:17.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر { ينسينك } بالتشديد وفعل وأفعل يجريان مجرى واحد كما بينا ذلك في مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers the common reading because 18:63 uses the related form in saying that Satan made the speaker forget.
rows.anchor: والاختيار قراءة العامة لقوله تعالى : { وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان } ( الكهف : 63 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If you forget and remain seated, do not stay after being reminded; get up once you remember.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية : إن نسيت وقعدت فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى ، وقم إذا ذكرت

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says dhikrā is a noun meaning reminder.
rows.anchor: والذكرى اسم للتذكرة قاله الليث

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says dhikrā can mean remembrance or mention.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : الذكرى يكون بمعنى الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers in this passage are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { مع القوم الظالمين } يعني مع المشركين
